parent_channels.active_motifs: camphor as perfume (quranic:root_001307:B011/m01); perfuming with aromatic spices (quranic:root_000933:B003/m01); perfume brazier (quranic:root_000973:B012/m01); coating with khaluq perfume (quranic:root_000434:B010/m01); sweet scent spreading outward (quranic:root_001503:B003/m01); receiving and distinguishing scent (quranic:root_000609:B004/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: An unseen fragrance made knowable by its spreading trace materializes the ascent of good speech in 35:10: an inwardly prepared quality leaves its source and becomes perceptible at a distance. The scene also reframes the winds of 35:9 as carriers whose effects disclose what ordinary sight cannot grasp directly.

parent_channels.name: S14. Whole Surah (35:1-45) From Fresh Meat to a Seasoned Meal
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Fresh meat passes to a butcher-cook, enters a cooking pot, receives a measured amount of salt, is served in a bowl, tasted, and eaten.
parent_channels.active_motifs: edible meat (quranic:root_001348:B001/m01); cooking pot and the butcher-cook who tends it (quranic:root_001205:B007/m01); salt added to food or pot (quranic:root_001442:B001/m01); eating bowl or vessel (quranic:root_000043:B013/m01); tasting food (quranic:root_000526:B001/m01); consuming food (quranic:root_000043:B001/m01)
parent_channels.ayah_anchors: 35:1 `قَدِيرٌ` (ق د ر); 35:12 `لَحْمًا/مِلْحٌ/تَأْكُلُ` (ل ح م/م ل ح/ء ك ل); 35:37 `ذُوقُ` (ذ و ق).
parent_channels.synthesis: The meal directly materializes the fresh meat and saline water of 35:12 as usable provision transformed by proportion, heat, vessel, taste, and ingestion. Provision in 35:3 is thereby pressured toward bodily dependence: possession is not nourishment until material passes through a skilled sequence and becomes consumable.

parent_channels.name: S15. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Singer, Answering Voice, Drum, and Cymbal
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A singer raises a melodic line, a second voice follows in response, a one-faced drum establishes pulse, a cymbal rings, and hearers receive the coordinated performance.
parent_channels.active_motifs: song and melodic voice (quranic:root_001110:B003/m01); raised-voice song (quranic:root_001507:B009/m01); answering voice following a singer (quranic:root_000186:B007/m01); one-faced drum (quranic:root_001281:B012/m01); ringing cymbal (quranic:root_000897:B009/m01); pleasurable hearing of song (quranic:root_000741:B007/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The ensemble usefully pressures the hearing contrasts of 35:14 and 35:22 by separating produced sound, patterned succession, instrumental reinforcement, and receptive hearing. Even loud, ordered, attractive sound does not complete communication unless an addressee can receive it, sharpening the surah's distinction between calling and making hear.

parent_channels.name: S16. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Maysir Arrows and Divided Shares
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Players collect marked arrows in a leather vessel, include the named fifth arrow, draw lots over a slaughtered camel, separate the resulting shares, and seek victory through a wager vulnerable to deception.
parent_channels.active_motifs: vessel holding maysir arrows (quranic:root_000532:B010/m01); fifth maysir arrow (quranic:root_001533:B016/m01); arrow gambling and division of a camel (quranic:root_001694:B007/m01); apportioning a share (quranic:root_001226:B003/m01); gambling victory through deception (quranic:root_001255:B007/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: This chance-based allocation usefully pressures the world's deception in 35:5 and the increase of loss in 35:39. A visible prize and formally divided shares generate expectation, but the concealed draw and adversarial wager make hoped-for gain structurally capable of becoming another's loss rather than reliable provision.

parent_channels.name: S17. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Offering, Destination, and Slaughter Boundary
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A vow binds its maker to an offering, a consecrated animal is directed toward the sanctuary, a rival rite redirects slaughter to an erected stone, and the boundary of proper slaughter distinguishes offering from carcass.
parent_channels.active_motifs: self-binding vow (quranic:root_001488:B002/m01); offering made to seek nearness to God (quranic:root_001212:B005/m01); consecrated animal sent to the sanctuary (quranic:root_001583:B005/m01); erected stone used for worship and slaughter (quranic:root_001507:B002/m01); edible animal dead without ritual slaughter (quranic:root_001454:B007/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The rite materializes the worship and obedience of 35:28-29 as a directed transfer of a valued body, while the rival slaughter-stone usefully pressures the false invocation of 35:13-14. Destination and authorized handling, not material expenditure alone, determine whether the act embodies nearness or diverts devotion toward a powerless recipient.

parent_channels.name: S18. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Herd at the Watering Turn
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A herder drives livestock to water, joins a drinking group with an assigned share, draws water at the camels' mouths, returns a still-thirsty animal for another drink, then leads the herd back at evening and encloses it in a pen.
parent_channels.active_motifs: driving livestock to water (quranic:root_000762:B001/m01); assigned water share (quranic:root_000783:B002/m01); group sharing a watering place (quranic:root_000783:B003/m01); drawing water at camels' mouths (quranic:root_001198:B014/m01); returning camels for a second drink (quranic:root_000464:B007/m01); evening return of livestock (quranic:root_000609:B005/m01); livestock pen (quranic:root_000897:B003/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The daily watering cycle reframes provision in 35:3 and human poverty in 35:15 as apportioned dependence: each body requires a share, repeated access, guidance to the source, and protected return. The scene also materializes divine sufficiency by contrast, since the herd's whole routine is organized around needs it cannot satisfy from itself.

parent_channels.name: S19. Cross-Pericope P1-P2-P3 Contested Right and Discharge
parent_channels.scene_or_process: P1 (35:1-14) supplies the written claim and chosen arbitrator; P2 (35:15-30) supplies the continuing right and release from liability; P3 (35:31-45) supplies collection and final discharge. Bridge: a shared legal invariant and causal sequence in which a contested right remains attached until it is documented, adjudicated, satisfied, and cleared.
parent_channels.active_motifs: opposing claims to the same right (quranic:root_000347:B004/m01); deed recording a right (quranic:root_000516:B008/m01); appointment of an arbitrator (quranic:root_000348:B005/m01); collecting a debt in full (quranic:root_000244:B003/m01); paying and receiving the due right (quranic:root_001237:B006/m01); release from liability (quranic:root_000436:B006/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The legal process materializes the non-transferable burden of 35:18, the full payment of 35:30, and the earned liability of 35:45 as stages of one attached claim. Its cross-pericope force lies in progression rather than topical recurrence: document and arbitration make the obligation legible, while collection and discharge determine whether it remains active.

parent_channels.name: S20. Cross-Pericope P1-P2-P3 Promise, Appointment, and Outcome
parent_channels.scene_or_process: P1 (35:1-14) establishes a promise and its appointed time or place; P2 (35:15-30) supplies attendance or default at the appointment; P3 (35:31-45) tests the promise by enacted confirmation. Bridge: a causal speech-act sequence with a terminal contrast between fulfillment and breach.
parent_channels.active_motifs: appointment fixing a promise in time or place (quranic:root_001662:B003/m01); reciprocal promise between parties (quranic:root_001662:B004/m01); arriving and assembling at the appointment (quranic:root_001669:B004/m01); making a promise true by action (quranic:root_000852:B004/m01); failure to keep the appointed promise (quranic:root_000433:B005/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The appointment scene sharpens the contrast between the true divine promise of 35:5 and the deceiver's promise of 35:40. A promise creates expectation, but only arrival and corresponding action verify it; breach reverses the speech act into evidence against its speaker, while fulfillment converts words into an encountered outcome.

parent_channels.name: S21. Cross-Pericope P1-P2-P3 Household Line and Estate
parent_channels.scene_or_process: P1 (35:1-14) supplies the household frame; P2 (35:15-30) supplies mother, following child, and remembered forebears; P3 (35:31-45) supplies surviving descendants and the estate left at death. Bridge: role progression and reversal across generations, as a dependent child becomes a forebear whose possessions and position pass into the surviving line.
parent_channels.active_motifs: household and kin group (quranic:root_000067:B003/m01); mother as bearer and nurturer (quranic:root_000053:B001/m01); child following its mother (quranic:root_000186:B006/m01); grandparents and ancestry (quranic:root_000227:B009/m01); surviving descendants (quranic:root_001033:B004/m01); estate left by the dead (quranic:root_000180:B006/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The household progression supports 35:11's creation, generation, and measured lifespan, then reframes the Book's inheritance in 35:32 and human succession in 35:39 at the scale of embodied family roles. Continuity belongs to the line rather than to any one holder: nurture produces followers, followers become forebears, and death turns possession into an estate for those who remain.

parent_channels.name: S22. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Udder Filling, Milking, and Drying
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Milk descends into an udder and fills it; a small remnant is left to draw down what follows, while the animal may retain the milk or release it in a continuing flow. A milker works with the fingertips until the supply is collected or dries up.
parent_channels.active_motifs: milk descending into the udder (quranic:root_000351:B009/m01); full udder and abundant milk (quranic:root_000810:B003/m01); remnant left to call down following milk (quranic:root_000478:B003/m01); milk held back in the udder (quranic:root_000582:B007/m01); continuous milk flow (quranic:root_000563:B006/m01); fingertip milking (quranic:root_001165:B005/m01); milk drying up or being cut off (quranic:root_000227:B011/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The bodily mechanism materializes the opening and withholding of 35:2 and the provision of 35:3 as a resource that can fill, remain retained, descend, and be gathered. The milker can coax and collect the flow but cannot originate lactation, preserving the surah's distinction between handling provision and creating it. The abundance sense of the gratitude root also links thanksgiving in 35:12 and 35:34 to experienced plenitude rather than bare verbal response.

parent_channels.name: S23. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Matched Proverb and Unequal Pair
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A speaker casts a saying as a proverb, places one case beside its counterpart, tests whether the two can be made equal, and leaves the comparison as a lesson or sign.
parent_channels.active_motifs: speech brought out in utterance (quranic:root_001272:B001/m01); proverb cast as a saying (quranic:root_001397:B003/m01); counterpart set beside counterpart (quranic:root_001520:B006/m01); equality tested between two things (quranic:root_000766:B001/m01); proverb retained as lesson and sign (quranic:root_001397:B011/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The scene supports the paired contrasts of 35:19-22 as a precise teaching operation: blindness is aligned with sight, darkness with light, shade with heat, and the living with the dead so that non-equivalence becomes the lesson. The likeness wording at 35:14 supplies the lexical hinge, while the repeated refusal of equality prevents analogy from flattening the opposed outcomes it is meant to disclose.

parent_channels.name: S24. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Benefaction, Thanks, and Repute
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A benefactor gives a good gift beyond strict equivalence; the recipient recognizes the favor, voices praise repeatedly, and helps a good name circulate. Ingratitude reverses the response by concealing the favor.
parent_channels.active_motifs: benefaction beyond bare justice (quranic:root_000323:B002/m01); generous gift (quranic:root_000452:B005/m01); recognizing favor and thanking its giver (quranic:root_000810:B001/m01); praise opposed to blame (quranic:root_000355:B001/m01); repeated commendation of good acts (quranic:root_000208:B010/m01); good repute spreading among people (quranic:root_000745:B008/m01); ingratitude as covering a favor (quranic:root_001307:B004/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: This response circuit supports the surah's movement from praise in 35:1 to the inhabitants' praise in 35:34 and the naming of God as Appreciative in 35:30. Favor becomes socially legible when it is acknowledged and retold; disbelief is the exact reversal, covering what was received and severing gift from giver. The scene therefore makes praise and ingratitude opposed operations on one benefaction rather than unrelated religious labels.

parent_channels.name: S25. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Obscured Riddle and Hidden-Hand Reveal
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A challenger deliberately obscures a meaning in a riddle, keeps its object in the hand, and requires the other player to bring the hidden thing out. The response succeeds by production and disclosure rather than unsupported assertion.
parent_channels.active_motifs: riddling challenge with an obscured answer (quranic:root_000478:B007/m01); deliberate obscuring and confusion of meaning (quranic:root_001049:B004/m01); hand as the concealing and presenting limb (quranic:root_001693:B001/m01); game of bringing out what is held in the hand (quranic:root_000400:B010/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The game usefully pressures the demand in 35:40 to show what the alleged partners created. A riddle can hide a real answer in a hand and end when the object is produced; the claimants, by contrast, cannot disclose a created object because none is held. Against 35:38, the scene also distinguishes human guessing under concealment from knowledge that already reaches what chests hide.

parent_channels.name: S26. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Whorl-Bead Charm and Counter-Rite
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A rounded, whorl-like bead is hung as a charm; an incantation claims to restrain a person or turn the person's face toward another, while a counter-rite is performed to release the affliction.
parent_channels.active_motifs: spindle whorl supplying the rounded charm form (quranic:root_001177:B005/m01); face-turning bead used by a sorceress (quranic:root_001198:B016/m01); restraining incantation or charm (quranic:root_000018:B004/m01); counter-incantation that removes an affliction (quranic:root_001503:B008/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The source-attested rite usefully pressures the deceiver's attractive promise in 35:5-8 and the appeal to powerless recipients in 35:13-14. Its claimed influence is routed through a visible token, binding speech, and an answering release rite; the surah's primary claim denies such invoked intermediaries independent possession or response. The counter-rite sense of spreading also reframes resurrection at 35:9 as an unbinding that no talisman performs.

parent_channels.name: S27. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Written Manumission by Installments
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A person is held as transferable property under an owner's control; a written contract fixes staged payments, and completion changes the person's legal status from enslavement to freedom.
parent_channels.active_motifs: enslaved person held as property (quranic:root_000973:B001/m01); ownership and power of disposal (quranic:root_001444:B002/m01); manumission contract with installment terms (quranic:root_001283:B005/m01); freedom and release from bondage (quranic:root_000306:B002/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The contract materializes ownership, writing, payment, and release as a single status-changing practice. It usefully pressures the ownership claim at 35:13: contingent human title can be documented, transferred, and terminated, while the invoked partners possess not even the date-stone membrane. The Book-bearing servants of 35:31-32 are therefore not equated with chattel; the scene instead exposes how limited every created ownership arrangement is beside the surah's account of divine possession and human dependence.

parent_channels.name: S28. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Ostrich Nest, Chick, and Abandoned Egg
parent_channels.scene_or_process: An ostrich pair uses a shallow ground scrape, lays an egg, and opens a reproductive fork toward a living chick or an egg left abandoned in open country.
parent_channels.active_motifs: ostrich ground nest (quranic:root_000148:B012/m01); ostrich as the parent bird (quranic:root_001525:B006/m01); male ostrich (quranic:root_000967:B006/m01); bird egg (quranic:root_000168:B003/m01); ostrich chick (quranic:root_000248:B010/m01); ostrich egg abandoned in the wilderness (quranic:root_000180:B008/m01)
parent_channels.synthesis: The exposed nesting scene materializes the generation and measured life of 35:11 as a vulnerable transition from parent to egg to chick rather than an automatic continuity. Its abandoned-egg outcome gives concrete pressure to 35:45, where comprehensive seizure would leave no creature: what is left behind in ordinary reproduction remains fully within the reach of the final claim.

parent_channels.name: S29. Whole Surah (35:1-45) Wasting Illness, Recovery, and Relapse
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Illness takes hold of a body and wastes its flesh; the patient begins to recover, returns toward a former condition, and appears restored, but a relapse can return the disease or wound to a worse state.
parent_channels.active_motifs: illness taking hold in the body (quranic:root_000018:B007/m01); wasting disease that strips flesh (quranic:root_000086:B011/m01); convalescence after emaciation (quranic:root_000152:B003/m01); return toward a better bodily condition (quranic:root_000544:B014/m01); recovery and renewed likeness after illness (quranic:root_001397:B012/m01); relapse after improvement (quranic:root_001096:B004/m01)
parent_channels.ayah_anchors: 35:6, 35:26, 35:45 `ٱتَّخِذُ/أَخَذْ/يُؤَاخِذُ` (ء خ ذ); 35:12 `بَحْرَانِ` (ب ح ر); 35:4 `تُرْجَعُ` (ر ج ع); 35:14 `مِثْلُ` (م ث ل); 35:7, 35:28, 35:30, 35:34, 35:41 `مَّغْفِرَةٌ/غَفُورٌ/غَفُورًا` (غ ف ر). The surface root ب ل ل is unavailable in the bundle, so its convalescence motif cannot receive a token-level anchor.
parent_channels.synthesis: This reversible bodily course usefully pressures the surah's two terminal dwellings. Ordinary relief may follow wasting and still relapse; by contrast, fatigue cannot reach the settled inhabitants in 35:35, while the punishment of 35:36 is neither ended by death nor lightened into convalescence. The relapse sense attached to the forgiveness root sharpens permanent relief as more than a temporary improvement.
